verses.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
“If someone dares to say something to you, will it upset you? But who can keep quiet?
Look, you’ve taught many people and strengthened hands that had gone weak.
Your words held up people who were about to fall. You steadied knees that were giving way.
But now trouble’s come for you, and you’re worn out. It touches you, and you’re shaken.
Isn’t your reverence for God what gives you confidence? Isn’t the way you’ve lived with integrity what gives you hope?
“Think about it. Who ever died while innocent? Where were upright people ever cut down?
Here’s what I’ve seen: people who plow up wrongdoing and plant trouble harvest the same thing.
God’s breath wipes them out. A blast of his anger consumes them.
The lion’s roar, the fierce lion’s growl, and the young lions’ teeth are all broken.
The old lion dies for lack of prey, and the lioness’s cubs scatter.
“Something came to me in secret. I caught just a whisper of it.
As I thought about visions in the night, when people fall into deep sleep,
fear and trembling came over me. Every bone in my body shook.
A spirit passed in front of my face, and the hair on my body stood up.
It stopped, but I couldn’t make out what it looked like. A shape stood before my eyes. There was silence, and then I heard a voice:
‘Can a mortal be more just than God? Can a person be more pure than their Maker?
Look, God doesn’t put his trust in his servants. He finds fault even with his angels.
How much less can he trust those who live in houses of clay, with foundations in the dust, who are crushed before a moth!
Between morning and evening they’re destroyed. They’re gone for good, and nobody even notices.
Isn’t their tent cord pulled up from within them? They die without gaining wisdom.’”
